findings.title: Belief accompanies the striving
findings.claim: The circumstantial wa places the believing state alongside the same person's striving, rather than adding belief as a later event.
findings.mechanism: The conjunction at 17:19:7:1 introduces the nominal clause huwa mu'min at 17:19:7:2 and 17:19:8:1; that state qualifies the already named effort while it is being described.
findings.reader_payoff: Belief is perceived as the condition in which the work is carried out.
findings.containment: The clause establishes accompaniment within this condition; it does not settle a chronology of inward belief or turn faith into a separate action.

epistemic.reason: The focus QAC form and both trusted word-analysis supports identify the circumstantial conjunction and its local predicate.

findings.title: A state, not another action
findings.claim: The nominal clause presents belief as a standing quality of the conditional agent.
findings.mechanism: Huwa at 17:19:7:2 supplies an overt subject and mu'min at 17:19:8:1 predicates a quality without another finite verb; the circumstantial wa at 17:19:7:1 keeps the frame attached to the effort.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish the believing state from the two finite acts of willing and striving.
findings.containment: Standing describes the clause's presentation of the state here, not an assertion that the person never changes.

epistemic.reason: The nominal clause and its predicate are directly identified by trusted focus analysis.

findings.reader_payoff: The state of belief does not appear to belong to a second, newly introduced person.
findings.containment: The pronoun preserves local reference; it makes no claim about a wider group beyond the result clause.

epistemic.reason: The focus pronoun, clause attachment, and same-agent reference are supplied in trusted analysis.

findings.title: Willing as a completed condition
findings.claim: The perfect form presents willing as a completed act included in the conditional qualification.
findings.mechanism: Arada at 17:19:2:1 is governed by man at 17:19:1:2 and coordinated with the following striving; its perfect form packages the willing before fa opens the result.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence treats intention as a fulfilled condition within the rule, rather than an ongoing event in its result.
findings.containment: The contrast with the imperfect desire of 17:18 and the comparison with 17:16 are excluded; no temporal opposition beyond the focus form is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The perfect form is supplied; the settled-condition effect is a local aspectual reading.

findings.title: The afterlife directs present work
findings.claim: Al-akhirah names the end toward which the striving is directed, so the afterlife is a goal of action as well as the object of willing.
findings.mechanism: The definite object at 17:19:3:2 returns as the referent of laha at 17:19:5:1-2; the cognate measure at 17:19:6:1-2 then attaches the work's standard to that same end.
findings.reader_payoff: The final reality becomes the destination that gives present effort its direction.
findings.containment: This finding stays with the focus's afterlife object and its work relation; comparisons with 17:18, 17:7, 17:10, 17:72, and 17:104 are excluded.

epistemic.reason: The lexical reading and the local goal and measure relations are directly supported.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: ölümden sonraki yaşam ve öteki dünya

findings.title: One referent travels through the clause
findings.claim: The definite feminine object of willing remains the same referent in the later goal and effort-measure pronouns.
findings.mechanism: Al-akhirah at 17:19:3:2 is resumed by the governed ha at 17:19:5:2 and the feminine suffix at 17:19:6:2, carrying one object through willing, striving, and its measure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can track one final reality through the whole effort phrase rather than hearing the suffixes as new referents.
findings.containment: The adjacent and wider same-surah comparisons are excluded; the claim is local agreement and reference.

epistemic.reason: The definite object, feminine agreement, and suffix references are supplied by focus analysis.

findings.title: The goal supplies the measure
findings.claim: The final reality is not only the target of striving; the suffix on the effort measure makes it the standard belonging to that target.
findings.mechanism: The ha on sa'yaha at 17:19:6:2 agrees with the earlier al-akhirah and laha at 17:19:3:2 and 17:19:5:2, while the cognate accusative specifies the kind of work.
findings.reader_payoff: The effort is measured in relation to the end it claims to seek.
findings.containment: This does not prescribe a separate practical rule or deny other meanings of the final reality; wider context comparisons are excluded.

epistemic.reason: The suffix and cognate construction are supplied; construing the goal as the effort's standard is an interpretive relation.

findings.title: Effort joins intention as a condition
findings.claim: The inner wa adds striving to willing as a cumulative requirement inside the same conditional.
findings.mechanism: Wa at 17:19:4:1 coordinates the second perfect verb sa'a at 17:19:4:2 with arada at 17:19:2:1 under man at 17:19:1:2.
findings.reader_payoff: Desire for the end does not by itself complete the condition; enacted effort is added before belief and result.
findings.containment: The conjunction joins requirements without ranking them or making them synonyms.

epistemic.reason: The coordination and shared conditional scope are directly supplied.

findings.title: Effort has a destination
findings.claim: Sa'a is a qualifying act of striving directed through laha toward the named final reality.
findings.mechanism: The perfect verb at 17:19:4:2 stays within the open condition; the following lam and feminine pronoun at 17:19:5:1-2 give its effort a goal relation rather than a direct object to seize.
findings.reader_payoff: Striving appears as enacted, goal-directed work rather than a free-standing virtue.
findings.containment: The cited comparison with 2:114 is excluded; this reading uses only the focus's own direction phrase.

epistemic.reason: The conditional verb and its prepositional goal are directly supported in the focus.

findings.title: Direction belongs to the evaluation
findings.claim: The verse makes direction part of the effort it evaluates: the striving is for the named final reality, not effort in the abstract.
findings.mechanism: The lam and feminine goal pronoun at 17:19:5:1-2 return to the object at 17:19:3:2, and the final predicate at 17:19:12:1 evaluates the class's striving at 17:19:11:1.
findings.reader_payoff: The goal and the positive appraisal meet in one focus-local relation, so the work's orientation matters to its result.
findings.containment: The contrast with misdirected striving at 2:114 is excluded; this does not claim that direction is the only condition in the ayah.

epistemic.reason: The local goal and final evaluation are explicit; their relation as a criterion is an interpretive synthesis.

findings.title: Movement and work remain together
findings.claim: The effort root keeps movement and labor fused, while the goal phrase makes that exertion purposeful.
findings.mechanism: Sa'a at 17:19:4:2 carries the motion-and-work field; laha at 17:19:5:1-2 turns it toward the final reality rather than leaving motion without direction.
findings.reader_payoff: Striving can be felt as embodied effort moving toward an end, not intention alone.
findings.containment: No literal travel scene or cross-ayah example at 2:114 is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The supplied root range and local goal phrase support this focus-local synthesis.

findings.title: Act, measure, evaluated work
findings.claim: The three focus occurrences of the effort root shift from an act, to its proper measure, to the effort that receives the final predicate.
findings.mechanism: Sa'a at 17:19:4:2 is the first act, sa'yaha at 17:19:6:1 is the cognate measure, and sa'yuhum at 17:19:11:1 becomes the evaluated subject.
findings.reader_payoff: The repetition builds a progression in which the work is carried forward and then appraised.
findings.containment: The chain is wholly within 17:19; the 2:114 contrast is excluded.

epistemic.reason: The three repeated focus forms and their changing grammatical roles are supplied.

findings.title: Target before measure
findings.claim: The goal is fixed before the ayah specifies the proper measure of striving.
findings.mechanism: Laha at 17:19:5:1-2 stands between sa'a and the cognate measure sa'yaha at 17:19:6:1-2, so the referent is named before the standard.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears what the effort is for before hearing what kind of effort is due.
findings.containment: This is an order and reference claim, not an assertion that the end is possessed or controlled by the striver.

epistemic.reason: The word order and bound referent are supplied in the focus.

findings.title: For it, not possession of it
findings.claim: Lam makes the striving for and toward the final reality, a relation of purpose rather than possession.
findings.mechanism: The preposition at 17:19:5:1 governs ha at 17:19:5:2 after sa'a at 17:19:4:2, directing the work to its referent.
findings.reader_payoff: The effort is oriented toward the end without making the end an object the striver controls.
findings.containment: Purpose, direction, and benefactive force coexist; no single English gloss exhausts the preposition.

epistemic.reason: The preposition's local governance and purpose relation are explicitly supplied.

findings.title: The bound pronoun returns to the goal
findings.claim: The feminine ha governed by lam returns to the afterlife object introduced by willing.
findings.mechanism: The suffix at 17:19:5:2 agrees with al-akhirah at 17:19:3:2 and is governed by the lam at 17:19:5:1, so it continues the existing referent as the goal of work.
findings.reader_payoff: The striving stays aimed at the same final reality rather than acquiring a new subject.
findings.containment: This local reference does not by itself establish every theological property of the referent.

epistemic.reason: The suffix's case relation and feminine agreement are directly supplied.

findings.title: The target returns as standard
findings.claim: The target is named in the goal phrase and then returns as the referent that owns the measure of striving.
findings.mechanism: Ha at 17:19:5:2 first identifies the goal; the second feminine suffix at 17:19:6:2 attaches the cognate measure to that same target.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader encounters the goal before hearing effort calibrated to it.
findings.containment: The two suffixes preserve one local referent; they do not add an unstated rule for measuring every act.

epistemic.reason: The repeated feminine suffix and word order are supplied by focus evidence.

findings.title: The repeated noun specifies the effort
findings.claim: Sa'yaha is a cognate accusative that specifies the kind or measure of striving rather than adding a second act.
findings.mechanism: The verbal noun at 17:19:6:1 repeats the root of sa'a at 17:19:4:2, and its accusative role makes the action itself more specific; its suffix links that measure to the goal.
findings.reader_payoff: The condition asks for effort of a fitting kind, not merely the existence of effort.
findings.containment: The construction specifies a measure without supplying a numerical quota.

epistemic.reason: The cognate accusative function and suffix are identified in the focus analysis.

findings.title: The middle occurrence calibrates effort
findings.claim: The second effort form shifts the repeated root from an act into its measure and prepares the final evaluated subject.
findings.mechanism: Sa'yaha at 17:19:6:1 follows sa'a at 17:19:4:2 and precedes sa'yuhum at 17:19:11:1; its cognate-accusative role creates the middle link.
findings.reader_payoff: The repeated root develops through changing grammatical work rather than repeating one idea unchanged.
findings.containment: The focus's three occurrences supply the sequence; no external example is needed.

epistemic.reason: The support names the three local occurrences and the second form's distinct role.

findings.title: The goal owns the measure
findings.claim: The suffix on sa'yaha lets the final reality define the measure of effort due toward it.
findings.mechanism: Ha at 17:19:6:2 is feminine like al-akhirah at 17:19:3:2 and resumes the earlier goal suffix at 17:19:5:2; its attachment makes the cognate measure belong to that referent.
findings.reader_payoff: The desired end supplies a standard for the striving directed to it.
findings.containment: Possessive and objective pressure coexist in the suffix; neither becomes a claim that the goal is literally owned.

epistemic.reason: The agreement and attachment are supplied; describing the target as the effort's standard is interpretive.

findings.title: The end governs the course of effort
findings.claim: The named later end sets both the direction and fitting measure of the work, so the verse presents intention as a course that must match what it seeks.
findings.mechanism: Arada at 17:19:2:1 turns toward al-akhirah at 17:19:3:2; sa'a at 17:19:4:2 and its repeated forms at 17:19:6:1 and 17:19:11:1 enact that orientation, while laha and sa'yaha at 17:19:5:1-2 and 17:19:6:1-2 bind the work and its measure to the end.
findings.reader_payoff: The work becomes more than effort in the abstract: its destination shapes what counts as fitting pursuit.
findings.containment: The wandering branch is only an attributed negative edge, not a literal animal scene. The word-analysis form restriction keeps arada at deliberate willing, not physical roaming; no wider context is used.

epistemic.reason: The HFT roles are legacy_unbound, but their coordinates agree with the focus surface and each proposed contact is bounded by supplied branch records.
